newsitem.title: USA: National Fuel trims 1st phase of expansion.
newsitem.headline: National Fuel trims 1st phase of expansion.

text.p: National Fuel Gas Supply Corp said Tuesday it has reduced the volume proposed for the first phase of its 1998-1999 Niagara Expansion Project and will seek approval of the expansion as two separate projects.

The National Fuel Gas Co subsidiary said it now anticipates submitting a filing with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission later next month for transportation of about 100 million cubic feet per day.
It had proposed a capacity of 300 million cubic feet daily for the first phase when proposing a two-phase project, spokeswoman Julie A. Coppola said.
Upon FERC's approval, the company said, it plans to start construction in the spring of 1998 and service in November.
National Fuel Gas said it expects a second project will bring at least an additional 400 million cubic feet per day from Canada to the Leidy Hub beginning in late 1999.

While the configuration of the Expansion Project has changed, the company said, it expects to ultimately achieve the same end result, the most economically feasible continuous transportation path from the producing regions in western Canada to the Ellisburg-Leidy Hub and the Eastern Seaboard markets it serves.
The revision is due to a delay in achieving a condition in one of the signed agreements for the project, the company explained without providing any details.
As a result, a new contract is being pursued.

A new Open Season for the second project will start May 1 to offer firm transportation service from the established Canadian import point of Niagara to the Ellisburg-Leidy Hub, National Fuel Gas said.
The hub accesses 6 billion cubic feet per day of pipeline capacity and 166 billion cubic feet of storage.

The proposed expansion of between 400 and 650 million cubic feet daily beginning in 1999 will be provided at rates comparable to or lower than those offered in the 1998 expansion and competitive with other recently announced pipeline projects, the company said.
If market support warrants, it added, the project can be expanded incrementally with a significant reduction in rates.
